messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: P1 - Partial regional connectivity degradation in us-west-2 affecting dual-stack endpoints. Symptoms: increased 5xx on v6 flows, long tail latencies on some control-plane calls. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

kbarker: seeing spikes in 502/504s on the healthcheck dashboard for edge-lb-usw2-v2. IPv4 looks fine, IPv6 error rate up ~12% for last 8m.

jchen: confirmed. Metrics: backend success rate v6 86%, v4 99%. TCP resets from clients on ports 443/80.

maria_sre: @netops can you pull v6 traceroutes from our egress in us-west-2 to one of the failing customer IPs? suspect PMTUD/MTU issue.

netops: running traceroute6 -> sample client (2001:db8:aaa::55):
``` 
traceroute to 2001:db8:aaa::55, 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  2600:1f18:xxxx::1  0.243 ms 0.211 ms 0.201 ms
 2  2600:1f18:xxxx::2  0.478 ms 0.447 ms 0.432 ms
 3  * * *
 4  2001:db8:transit::1  !P  25.412 ms 25.397 ms 25.392 ms
``` 
Note: hop 3 is dropping ICMPv6 TTL/exceeded and hop 4 returns "!P" (packet too big).

jchen: that !P looks like PMTUD telling us path MTU smaller than our packet. Are we sending jumbo frames internally? Any recent MTU changes on TGW/Transit?

dlee: we pushed a config change to enable jumbo frames on us-west-2a ENIs earlier today for a throughput test (mtu 9000). rolling back now.

kbarker: pls confirm whether the cloud transit/peer path honors ICMPv6 Packet Too Big. If ICMPv6 is filtered by a 3rd-party transit, PMTUD will fail and TCP will stall.

netops: we checked upstream peering — one transit peer is rate-limiting ICMPv6 and might be dropping PTB messages intermittently. Route path goes through that peer for some AZ->AZ cross-region traffic.

maria_sre: that matches: tcp dumps show repeated retransmits and MSS negotiation ok initially, but observed "Fragmentation needed and DF set" analog; basically hosts never reduce MSS.

jchen: quick mitigations we can do: 1) enable TCP MSS clamping on our NAT/edge to force MSS <= 1280 for v6 flows, 2) temporarily prefer IPv4 for affected ALB listeners (disable v6), 3) reroute traffic away from the transit peer. Which is fastest?

dlee: fastest is toggling ALB dualstack -> ipv4-only (can do per-target-group). I can push that for the most critical customer-facing routes in 5m. MSS clamping requires LB/NAT change; might be slightly riskier but doable.

kbarker: we should avoid widespread ALB toggles if possible, prefer MSS clamp on our egress NAT/edge so customers on dual-stack keep ipv6 but with safe MSS. Can you test MSS clamp in canary region?

netops: testing on a canary egress host now. tcpdump before/after shows client MSS 1452 -> forced 1240 after clamp. Re-run traceroute6 to client shows no !P and end-to-end connectivity restored.

maria_sre: good. Prepare rollout plan: 1) apply MSS clamp on all egress gateways in us-west-2, 2) monitor v6 success_rate, 3) if any regressions, fallback by toggling affected ALBs to ipv4-only.

incident-bot: Incident timeline updated. Priority: P1. Runbook step: network-mtu -> apply MSS clamp when PMTUD failures observed.

jchen: I'm going to open an emergency change for MSS clamp on the TGW route tables and NAT gateways (change ID CHG-2406). Estimated 10m to apply across 4 egress hosts, rolling.

dlee: applying on egress-1 now.

netops: post-change checks: v6 error rate down from 12% -> 1.2% for that canary prefix. Latency normalized.

kbarker: OK start rolling to the other 3 egress nodes. Coordinate with oncall-night for the handoff window. Keep changes rolling with 60s waits and healthchecks.

maria_sre: notifying support: we expect customer impacts to be limited to dual-stack IPv6-preferring clients. Most customers default to IPv4 so blast radius smaller.

oncall-night: acknowledged, will take over the stabilization window at shift change. Please summarize what to look for in handoff.

kbarker: handoff checklist for night oncall:
- change CHG-2406 status and which hosts updated
- watch metric: ipv6_success_rate (edge-lb-usw2-v2) threshold < 98% triggers rollback
- check tcp retransmit rate and tcp_established counts on egress hosts
- if MSS clamp causes unexpected failures for certain customers, fallback = toggle ALB -> ipv4-only for that route and open a ticket for netops to investigate transit peer.

maria_sre: Customer impact note for postmortem: A subset of customers with ipv6-preference and larger MTU paths experienced connection failures or long tail latency due to filtered ICMPv6 PTB messages on a transit peer combined with our internal use of jumbo frames in one AZ. Mitigation: rolled out TCP MSS clamping across us-west-2 egresses and removed jumbo frame config; final status: service restored to >99% for v6 flows.

jchen: contacting cloud provider support to confirm if they can remediate the transit peer or ensure ICMPv6 PTB is not filtered. Also asking whether their load balancer HW ever sends DF fragments that require PTB.

netops: provider acknowledged potential issue, assigned ticket AWS-INC-99872 to investigate downstream peer ICMPv6 handling.

dlee: rolling back the jumbo frames change on us-west-2a completed. Verified MTU at 1500 across ENIs.

kbarker: final action items before handoff: update incident doc, attach tcpdump/traceroute outputs, list affected customer prefixes, CHG-2406 change log. Also schedule postmortem with networking + infra.

oncall-night: got it — I'll monitor for 2h and escalate if ipv6_success_rate falls below 98%. If anything new, I'll re-open P1 and ping this channel.

maria_sre: thank you all. Initial RCA draft: combination of internal jumbo-frame config + filtered ICMPv6 PTB on an upstream transit peer -> PMTUD failure -> TCP stalls on IPv6. Mitigation: MSS clamp + revert jumbo frames; long-term: ensure PTB propagation, add egress path tests for PTB and consider ipv6-only regression tests in CI.

incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. All updates will be appended to the ticket. :white_check_mark:

kbarker: closing timeline notes. Will create the postmortem stub and assign owners for netops (fix peer), infra (hardening), and support (customer comms).

oncall-night: taking over monitoring. Leaving channel open.
